examples.problem: What set of parametric equations, defined for $t\in(-\infty, \infty),$ generates the horizontal parabola given by the Cartesian equation $y^2 = -64x?$
examples.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola $y^2=4px$ that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ are

$$
x = pt^2, \qquad y = 2pt,
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Comparing the given Cartesian equation with the general case $y^2=4px$ and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4px & =-64x \\ 4p & =-64 \\ p & =-16.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x = (-16)t^2, \qquad y = 2(-16)t,
$$

which simplify to

$$
x = -16t^2, \qquad y = -32t .
$$

feedback.problem: Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate a vertical parabola that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ and which passes through the point $(-7,-7)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a vertical parabola  that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ are

$$
x=2pt,\,y=p{t}^{2},
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Since the parabola passes through $(-7,-7),$ we can substitute $x=-7$ and $y=-7$ into the standard parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}-7=2pt \\ -7=p{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-7 & =2pt \\ t & =-\frac{7}{2p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-7 & =p{(-\frac{7}{2p})}^{2} \\ -7 & =p\cdot \frac{49}{4{p}^{2}} \\ -7 & =\frac{49}{4p} \\ 4p & =-7 \\ p & =-\frac{7}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x=2(-\frac{7}{4})t,\,y=(-\frac{7}{4}){t}^{2},
$$

which simplify to

$$
x=-\frac{7}{2}t,\,y=-\frac{7}{4}{t}^{2}.
$$
